attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, published as his view.

semantics.note: Correctly limited to the alienation clause, with 'this' read as Trump's escalation. 'Will almost certainly' states high confidence in a definite outcome, so under policy it is a scored forecast, not a hedge. No deadline was given.

contract.note: The contract treats 'almost certainly' as a hedge and sets the axis to not_applicable. Policy counts high-confidence language as a scored forecast. The contract also gives no plain reading of 'a large part of Silicon Valley', so whether the claim can be scored depends on that reading choice.

evidence.note: OpenAI disclosure dated 2026-02-28. It shows one major firm opposing the designation while still working with the government. A single company's position cannot show that a large part of Silicon Valley was alienated.

reviews.rationale: This is a high-confidence forecast with no deadline. The only evidence is one company's statement opposing the designation while it kept cooperating with the government. That falls short of showing a large part of the Valley was alienated, and it does not contradict the forecast either. With no deadline and no conclusive event, the forecast cannot be scored yet, so the outcome is unresolved.
